name: IAMGOLD Corporation
moat_justification: A gold miner is a pure price taker — no pricing power, no switching costs, no network effects; the only candidate advantages are cost position, reserve life and jurisdiction, and IAMGOLD is mid-pack on all three. ROIC proxy (fundamentals.json) ran -3.7% / 1.2% / -0.0% for FY2021-23 and only reached 20.1% / 18.5% in FY2024-25 when the gold price surged — below the cost of capital through most of the cycle. Gross margin expanded 7.1% (FY2021) to 42.3% (FY2025) on the gold price and the Côté ramp, not on anything the company controls. Côté Gold is a genuinely large, long-life Ontario asset, but consolidated AISC was $2,271/oz in Q2 2026 (company release) and roughly half of attributable production sits at Essakane in Burkina Faso.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 6.7%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 40-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Form 40-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18, SEC EDGAR form40f.htm, CIK 1203464), cover page: securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) are 'Common Shares, no par value', trading symbol IAG, New York Stock Exchange, with 591,144,545 shares outstanding as of period end — exactly the engine's DEI count; the NYSE security is the common share itself, not an ADS) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
one_liner: Price-taking gold miner, moat 3/10 — Tier F: no positive normalized owner's earnings (3-yr median OE/share -$0.14; OE positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years, the median window carrying Côté construction capex), so the OE DCF produces no IV and no price clears a 15% hurdle on normalized numbers; FY2025 alone earned $1.45/share and H1 2026 is running hotter at $4,631/oz YTD realized gold, so the $18.09 price is a bet on gold-price persistence and Côté's ramp, not on through-cycle earnings power.
moat_for: Côté Gold (70%, Ontario): large long-life open pit now at nameplate throughput, with the Côté-Gosselin expansion as organic upside
Westwood (100%, Quebec): high-grade underground mine in a tier-1 jurisdiction
Balance sheet transformed post-ramp: net cash at June 30, 2026 with an undrawn revolver (Q2 2026 release), and buybacks begun — 21.5M shares repurchased in H1 2026 (interim statements)
moat_against: Pure commodity price taker: earnings are a leveraged function of the gold price; the FY2025 base year was earned at peak-cycle prices
ROIC proxy below the cost of capital through most of the cycle: -3.7% / 1.2% / -0.0% in FY2021-23 (fundamentals.json), positive only in the FY2024-25 gold surge
Mid-pack cost position: consolidated AISC $2,271/oz sold in Q2 2026 (company Q2 2026 release)
Essakane (85%, Burkina Faso) supplies roughly half of attributable production — junta and security jurisdiction risk
Depleting assets must be replaced with heavy capex: $907.3M of capex in FY2023 alone; owner's earnings positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years
Dilution record: diluted share count compounding at 6.7%/yr (engine) to fund the Côté build-out
